title: Tsadi Hebrew Letter (צ): Tzaddi, Sound & Final Tsadi
description: Learn the Hebrew letter Tsadi (צ), also spelled Tzaddi or Tsade: its [ts] sound, final Tsadi (ץ), words like צֵל (shadow) and interactive practice.

3.label: Tsadi Sofit
3.equivalent: Final Tsadi: Tsadi with its stem extended straight down below the line, written at the end of a word and pronounced [ts].

blocks.0: Tsadi Hebrew Letter (צ): Sound, Final Tsadi & Practice
blocks.9: The Hebrew word 'צֵל' [tsel] means 'shadow'. It has two letters: Tsadi (צ) and Lamed (ל). The Tsere (ֵ) beneath Tsadi gives [e], and Lamed gives [l]. Say tsel as one syllable, with a steady e; no special vowel length is required.
blocks.13: Read each word aloud. גַּן [gan], 'garden', has one syllable. בִּטָּחוֹן [bi-ta-chon], 'security', has three syllables, with the stress on chon; the dagesh in Tet does not require a doubled t in modern Hebrew. מְהֵרָה [me-he-ra], 'quickly', is a literary word: in this careful reading, the initial Sheva is read as e, giving three syllables with the stress on ra; a reduced two-syllable reading, [mhe-ra], is also used. אָבַד [a-vad] means 'he/it was lost', a past-tense verb form; it has two syllables, with the stress on vad. פּוֹעַל [po-al] means 'verb' in grammar; it has two syllables, with the stress on po. Keep o and a separate. Also review חֶבֶל [che-vel], 'rope': two syllables, with the stress on che. In חֶבֶל, Bet without a dagesh gives [v].

1.tip: Tsadi Sofit (ץ) is the final form of the same letter, Tsadi (צ).

4.tip: Use the regular form צ in the middle and Tsadi Sofit (ץ) at the end.

7.tip: Both forms represent [ts], like ts in 'cats'.

11.tip: Tsadi Sofit (ץ) is the final form; the regular form צ is used at the beginning or in the middle.

14.tip: A dagesh in Tsadi does not require you to pronounce a doubled consonant in ordinary modern Hebrew.

theory.heading: Meet Tsadi
theory.intro: The eighteenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet. Tsadi, also spelled Tzaddi, Tzadi or Tsade, makes a [ts] sound, as in “cats.” It is the last of the five letters with a final form: at the end of a word, Tsadi is written as Tsadi Sofit (ץ), with the same [ts] sound.
objectives: Recognize Tsadi: <bdi class="hebrew" lang="he" dir="rtl">צ</bdi>, and its final form, <bdi class="hebrew" lang="he" dir="rtl">ץ</bdi>.
Read Tsadi in real words like <bdi class="hebrew" lang="he" dir="rtl">צֵל</bdi> (shadow) and <bdi class="hebrew" lang="he" dir="rtl">חֵפֶץ</bdi> (object).

examples.heading: Tsadi in real words
examples.intro: See where each form of Tsadi goes, then read three words with Tsadi and five reading-practice words aloud. Hyphens in the transcriptions separate syllables.
